scripts.//build: Nothing to compile — the app is server-rendered with no bundler. This exists because Hostinger's Express preset runs `npm run build` during deploy, and a missing script exits non-zero and fails the deployment with npm install as the last thing in the log.
scripts.build: node -e "console.log('no build step: server-rendered, no bundler')"
scripts.//env: --env-file-if-exists, not --env-file. README tells you to copy .env.example to .env and run npm start; nothing loaded it, so `npm run migrate` answered 'not configured' on a correctly filled-in file and every local run needed the flag typed by hand. IF-EXISTS is the half that matters in production: on Hostinger the variables come from the Web App panel and there is no .env on disk, and plain --env-file exits non-zero on a missing file — which would turn a working deploy into a boot loop.
scripts.//test: Unqualified `node --test` discovers every *.test.js in the repo (node_modules excluded by default). The old "lib/*.test.js" glob would have skipped tests/wiring.test.js in silence — a test file nobody runs is worse than no test file, because it reads as covered.
